{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows sustained negative sentiment (e.g., multiple -0.25 or 0.00 values), indicating market pessimism.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5-7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, as true outcomes often converge toward historical mean.",
    "If forecast spikes upward after a negative sentiment period, apply a downward correction of 5-15% to prevent overreaction.",
    "When sentiment history includes a recent positive spike (e.g., 0.50 or 0.67), increase forecast sensitivity to recent high prices but cap upward adjustments to avoid overshoot.",
    "Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is significantly above 30-day average of recent 10-15 days, reduce by 2-5% per day until convergence.",
    "For long-term forecasts (e.g., 30-day horizon), reduce forecast bias toward extreme highs or lows if sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., alternating 0.00/0.33).",
    "If sentiment history shows a recent 0.00/0.33 pattern, expect a 1-3 day lag in true outcome, so adjust forecast to be 5-10% lower than model output for the next 2-3 days."
  ]
}
